sections.overview: The common greenshank is a migratory Eurasian wader, breeding in northern wetlands and wintering from western Europe to Africa and farther south and east.
sections.identification: It is a large, long-legged wader with greenish legs, a slightly upturned bill and a white rump; it lacks the broad white wing-bar of the common redshank.
sections.habitat: It breeds on the ground near water in northern moors and tundra; on migration it uses a range of freshwater and coastal wetlands.
sections.diet: It hunts aquatic insects and small fish in shallow water, sometimes walking or swimming as it searches.
sections.behavior: Its repeated three-note call is often heard during autumn passage through British wetlands.
sections.reproduction: It lays usually four eggs in a simple ground nest; both parents incubate and lead the downy young to water.
sections.ecology: The spotted redshank is among its close relatives in phylogenetic summaries; see that profile for a comparison of plumage and migration.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment is Least Concern; in Britain it is amber-listed, a regional conservation category.
